text:
Anya M: Quick check — onboarding results for argus-13b. We ran int6 and int8 quant on the longform summarization workload (avg input+output ~1.2k tokens). int8 gives ~34% token cost reduction but we see an avg ROUGE-L drop of 3.2% and some repetition/hallucination spikes in the tail (>800-token outputs). Planning: route longform to int6 or holdback a % for product validation? :thinking:

Kai L: What was the sample size and did you run human eval? If it's mostly tail behavior maybe it's KV-cache or attention truncation interacting with quantization.

Anya M: Sample: 2,000 longform prompts, A/B controlled. Human pairwise eval n=300 -> int6 preferred 58% vs int8 42% (p~0.04). Metrics: ROUGE-L -3.2, BLEU -1.1, hallucination rate +2.5ppt on int8 (measured by labeler pass).

Samir: Unit econ quick calc: int6 ~= $0.12 per 1k output tokens, int8 ~= $0.079 per 1k output tokens -> ~$41 savings per 1M tokens (~34%). For a product at 2M tokens/day that's ~ $82k/mo savings if fully switched. But that goods-vs-risk tradeoff is real for long content.

Rachel: Latency/throughput differences? Is int8 materially faster for p50/p95?

Kai L: int8 reduced p50 by ~10% on our bench; p95 mostly unchanged (kvcache and IO dominate). So perf wins are modest; cost is biggest driver.

Anya M: eval-bot table below (short):

eval-bot: |metric|int6|int8|delta|
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|ROUGE-L|42.1|38.9|-3.2|
|BLEU|12.3|11.2|-1.1|
|Hallucination rate|4.8%|7.3%|+2.5pp|
|Cost per 1k tokens|$0.12|$0.079|-34%|

Samir: Given that, my recommendation is conservative: default to int8 for cost, but route any request with expected output_tokens>800 to int6. Also start with a 20% holdback to surface product impact (GTN + retention).

Anya M: Proposed routing policy (2-week canary):

```json
{"priority_routing":[{"condition":"output_tokens>800","model":"argus-13b-int6"},{"condition":"default","model":"argus-13b-int8"}],"holdback_pct":20,"fallback":"argus-13b-int6"}
```

Checkpoints: 1) human NPS sample on summaries, 2) automated ROUGE-L drift alert if delta > 1.5 on the canary slices, 3) hallucination rate monitor.

Samir: +1. Also suggest initial GTN canary 5% for a few days then expand to 20% holdback. Keep the fallback aggressive (immediate switch to int6) if hallucination rate crosses +1pp vs baseline.

Rachel: I'll sync with Product tomorrow and set up a small user panel (qual) next Wed to see perceived summarization quality.

Anya M: Great — I'll file the scorecard (slices: long-article, multi-paragraph, instruction-heavy) and create dashboards for ROUGE-L / hallucination / cost. Rolling flag name: argus-13b-routing-v1. Staging rollout tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:
